title: Bézout's Identity in Bézout Rings: The Minimal Hypothesis
description: Answers the parent's open question: the GCD complete characterization ∃ x y, ax + by = c ↔ gcd(a,b) ∣ c generalizes from EuclideanDomain all the way to any commutative Bézout ring [CommRing R] [IsBezout R]. This drops the Euclidean algorithm, Noetherianity/PID structure, the integral-domain axiom, and DecidableEq/GCDMonoid. The mechanism is Mathlib's abstract gcd IsBezout.gcd (a generator of the principal ideal span{a,b}) and the ideal-theoretic Bézout witness IsBezout.gcd_eq_sum, replacing the concrete gcd_eq_gcd_ab. Also proves span{a,b} = span{gcd(a,b)} and IsCoprime a b ↔ IsUnit (gcd a b). 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: A Bézout ring (after Étienne Bézout, 1764) is a commutative ring in which every finitely generated ideal is principal — equivalently, every pair of elements admits a linear-combination gcd. This is a strictly weaker condition than being a principal ideal domain: Bézout rings need not be Noetherian and need not be integral domains. Classic Bézout domains that are not Euclidean (indeed not even Noetherian) include valuation rings and the ring of all algebraic integers. The parent entry proved the GCD complete characterization for Euclidean domains and explicitly asked whether the correct level of abstraction is instead IsBezout, and what the minimal typeclass is. This entry settles both questions.
overview.problemStatement:
**Question** (parent OQ-04-OQ-02 open questions): Can the GCD complete characterization be stated for IsBezout domains instead of EuclideanDomain? What is the minimal Mathlib typeclass for which linear_combination_iff_gcd_dvd holds?

**Answer**: YES, and the minimal hypothesis is `[CommRing R] [IsBezout R]` — even weaker than a Bézout *domain*, since no IsDomain axiom is needed.
overview.text: Reformulates Bézout's identity and the GCD characterization using Mathlib's abstract Bézout-ring gcd. Where the parent relied on the concrete extended-Euclidean coefficients (gcd_eq_gcd_ab), this entry uses the ideal-theoretic Bézout witness IsBezout.gcd_eq_sum, so the entire development goes through with only [CommRing R] [IsBezout R].
overview.proofStrategy:
Three ingredients replace the Euclidean machinery:

1. **IsBezout.gcd a b** is a generator of the principal ideal span{a,b} (well-defined via the span_pair_isPrincipal instance).
2. **gcd_dvd_left / gcd_dvd_right** give the forward direction (gcd divides every combination).
3. **IsBezout.gcd_eq_sum** gives the backward direction (gcd is itself a combination), reoriented by `ring` so coefficients sit on the right.

The complete characterization then follows by simp_rw exactly as in the parent, and two corollaries fall out: span{a,b} = span{gcd(a,b)} (one line from span_gcd) and IsCoprime ↔ gcd is a unit (via isUnit_iff_dvd_one and the main equivalence).
keyInsights: **Minimal hypothesis is [CommRing R] [IsBezout R]**: the characterization needs neither IsDomain, nor Noetherianity, nor a Euclidean algorithm, nor DecidableEq/GCDMonoid. Every Euclidean domain, every PID, and every valuation ring is covered simultaneously.

**Ideal-theoretic gcd**: IsBezout.gcd a b is defined as a *generator of span{a,b}* — noncomputable and only unique up to units. This is what lets the argument bypass the extended Euclidean algorithm the parent used.

**Structural essence — span_pair_eq_span_gcd**: span{a,b} = span{gcd(a,b)} says the ideal of all linear combinations is principal. This is precisely the property IsBezout asserts and precisely what fails in ℤ[X] (a UFD with gcd(2,X)=1 but 1 ∉ {2f+Xg}).
**Coprimality**: isCoprime_iff_gcd_isUnit repackages the main equivalence at c = 1 — a and b are coprime exactly when their gcd is a unit.
**Why not just a UFD**: the linear-combination (Bézout) property is strictly stronger than unique factorization; IsBezout is exactly the class where gcds are linear combinations.

sections.title: Module Header and Setup
sections.summary: Block comment (lines 1-30) stating the parent's open question and the answer: the minimal hypothesis is [CommRing R] [IsBezout R]. Lines 32-38: import Mathlib, namespace, variable {R} [CommRing R] [IsBezout R], and open IsBezout to expose gcd, gcd_dvd_left, gcd_eq_sum, span_gcd.
sections.mathContext: open IsBezout brings the abstract Bézout-ring gcd and its universal-property lemmas into scope. The span_pair_isPrincipal instance (from [IsBezout R]) makes IsBezout.gcd a b well-defined for every pair a, b.

sections.title: Part I: Core Lemmas
sections.summary: gcd_dvd_linear_combination (gcd ∣ ax + by, from gcd_dvd_left/right) and gcd_achievable_Bezout (∃ x y, ax + by = gcd, reorienting IsBezout.gcd_eq_sum with ring).
sections.mathContext: The forward direction uses only that gcd divides a and b. The Bézout witness gcd_eq_sum provides coefficients u, v with u·a + v·b = gcd; ring flips them to the a·x + b·y convention.

sections.title: Part II: Main Characterization
sections.summary: linear_combination_iff_gcd_dvd (∃ x y, ax+by=c ↔ gcd(a,b) ∣ c) and gcd_complete_characterization_Bezout (d ∼ gcd(a,b) ↔ achievability + universality).
sections.mathContext: Backward direction: from gcd ∣ c write c = gcd·k, expand gcd = u·a + v·b, so c = a·(k·u) + b·(k·v). The complete characterization is obtained by simp_rw with the divisibility equivalence, identical in shape to the parent.

sections.title: Part III: Corollaries
sections.summary: gcd_characterizes_ideal, span_pair_eq_span_gcd (span{a,b} = span{gcd(a,b)}), and isCoprime_iff_gcd_isUnit (IsCoprime a b ↔ IsUnit (gcd a b)).
sections.mathContext: span_pair_eq_span_gcd is (IsBezout.span_gcd a b).symm — the ideal of linear combinations is principal. The coprimality corollary rewrites isUnit as ∣ 1 and applies the main equivalence at c = 1, converting between u·a+v·b and a·x+b·y by ring.

sections.title: Part IV: Placement in the Algebraic Hierarchy
sections.summary: Three inferInstance examples: EuclideanDomain → IsBezout (subsumes the parent), IsPrincipalIdealRing → IsBezout (no IsDomain needed), and ValuationRing → IsBezout (a genuinely non-Euclidean, possibly non-Noetherian witness).
sections.mathContext: These document that the single [CommRing R] [IsBezout R] statement covers ℤ, ℚ[X], ℤ[i], all PIDs, and all valuation rings at once. Valuation rings of non-discrete valuations are Bézout but not Noetherian, hence not Euclidean domains.

sections.title: Part V: Concrete Examples in ℤ and Summary
sections.summary: Four ℤ witnesses (which avoid the noncomputable gcd): 6·(-2)+15·1=3; 6 achievable; 4 NOT achievable (omega); every integer is a combination of coprime 7 and 5. Closing Summary block and #check of the four headline theorems.
sections.mathContext: omega discharges non-achievability of 4 from {6,15} via the mod-3 obstruction. The coprime witness (3c, -4c) gives 7·(3c)+5·(-4c) = c by ring.

conclusion.summary: The GCD complete characterization ∃ x y, ax+by=c ↔ gcd(a,b) ∣ c holds in any commutative Bézout ring [CommRing R] [IsBezout R] — the minimal hypothesis, strictly weaker than the parent's EuclideanDomain and even weaker than a Bézout domain (no IsDomain). Mathlib's abstract gcd IsBezout.gcd and the witness IsBezout.gcd_eq_sum replace the Euclidean algorithm. Corollaries: span{a,b} = span{gcd(a,b)} and IsCoprime a b ↔ IsUnit (gcd a b). 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications:
**Correct level of abstraction**: this pins down IsBezout (not EuclideanDomain, not UFD) as exactly the hypothesis making Bézout's identity available. UFD is too weak (ℤ[X]); Euclidean domain and PID are stronger than necessary.

**Generality**: one theorem now covers ℤ, ℚ[X], Gaussian integers, all PIDs, and all valuation rings — including non-Noetherian Bézout rings with no Euclidean function.
openQuestions: Can span_pair_eq_span_gcd be extended from pairs to finite lists, giving span{a₁,…,aₙ} = span{gcd of the list} in a Bézout ring?
Is there a constructive/decidable version of IsBezout.gcd for specific Bézout rings (e.g. valuation rings of a computable valuation), or is noncomputability essential?
